units.text: okx-defi owns multi-chain OKX-aggregated DeFi products and positions: generic or venue-agnostic yield/APY/TVL discovery and history; deposits, staking, liquidity add/remove, withdrawals/redeem, reward claims, lending (borrow/repay), CLMM/V3 liquidity analysis; DeFi portfolio/position views. Trigger phrases: earn yield, best APY, DeFi product, APY/TVL history, deposit, stake, withdraw, redeem, provide or remove liquidity, claim rewards, borrow or repay, CLMM, V3 liquidity charts, DeFi portfolio, DeFi holdings.

Named third-party DApp/protocol requests - including protocol-specific APY, TVL, volume, history or timeframe analysis - route to okx-dapp-discovery. Generic cross-protocol yield/APY/TVL and V3-liquidity analysis stays in okx-defi.
Token search / price / chart requests route to okx-dex-market (token/market domain), not okx-defi.
Spot swaps, wallet balances, login, contract calls and transaction broadcasts route to okx-agentic-wallet (DeFi flows call into it for balance check, signing and broadcasting).
Skill metadata: name okx-defi, license MIT, author okx, version "4.6.3", homepage https://web3.okx.com. The version is used only as the preflight --skill-version argument.
units.note: Version pin only feeds the obsolete installer preflight; lite targets CLI 4.6.3 via docs/DESIGN.md instead.

units.text: At the start of each thread, complete the checks in ../okx-agentic-wallet/_shared/preflight.md; if missing, read the local _shared/preflight.md.
units.note: Lite skill folder is self-contained; no installer preflight. Use `ocl doctor` for environment/egress/login diagnostics.

units.text: Load only the reference files required by the selected route (progressive disclosure).

Invest capability (invest.md) covers: discover/search DeFi products and best APY; product detail (APY, TVL, accepted tokens); deposit/stake/provide liquidity; withdraw/redeem a position (full or partial); claim rewards (platform / investment / V3 fee / bonus / unlocked principal); APY history, TVL history, V3 depth/price charts.
Portfolio capability (portfolio.md) covers: view DeFi positions/holdings overview; per-protocol position detail.

Exact parameters/return schemas: invest, shared-support (support-chains/support-platforms) and chart commands -> invest-cli-reference.md; positions commands -> portfolio-cli-reference.md. Errors/failed deposits/expired calldata -> invest-troubleshooting.md; errors/empty positions/address-format issues -> portfolio-troubleshooting.md.
units.note: In lite, exact flag syntax lives only in references/commands/defi.md; return-schema/field knowledge must be kept separately.

units.text: Typical chained flow: view positions (Portfolio) -> redeem or claim (Invest). When a request chains them, read both the portfolio and invest references.
The CLI resolves chain names automatically (e.g. ethereum -> 1, bsc -> 56, solana -> 501). DeFi-specific aliases are in the portfolio Chain Support table.

When the user does NOT provide a wallet address, resolve it from the Agentic Wallet BEFORE running any defi command: (1) `wallet status` -> check logged in, get active account; (2) `wallet addresses` -> addresses grouped by chain category (XLayer, EVM, Solana); (3) match to target chain: EVM chains -> EVM address, Solana -> Solana address, XLayer -> XLayer address. Apply before every invest and portfolio command.
If the user provides an explicit address, use it directly and skip wallet address resolution.

units.source: SKILL.md#Security > Address Resolution; references/portfolio.md#Step 2: Collect Parameters
units.text: If the wallet is not logged in, ask the user to log in first (-> okx-agentic-wallet) or to provide an address manually.
units.note: Lite login = upstream social-login link flow: `wallet login` -> loginUrl -> user completes on OKX web page on any device -> `wallet login --phase poll`.

units.text: If the user says "check all accounts" / "all wallets": `wallet balance --all` to get all account IDs, then for each account `wallet switch <id>` + `wallet addresses`.
Always confirm the resolved address with the user before proceeding if the account has multiple addresses of the same type.

The --address and chain parameters must be compatible: EVM addresses (0x...) only query EVM chains; Solana addresses (base58) only query solana. Never mix them - the API returns error 84019 (Address format error).

Address -> allowed chains: 0x... -> only EVM chains `ethereum,bsc,polygon,arbitrum,base,xlayer,avalanche,optimism,fantom,linea,scroll,zksync`; base58 -> only `solana`; Sui address -> only `sui`; Tron (T...) -> only `tron`; TON -> only `ton`.
If the user wants positions across both EVM and Solana, make TWO separate `defi positions` calls, each with its matching address.
The wallet address parameter for ALL defi commands is `--address`.
`defi positions` uses `--chains` (plural, comma-separated, e.g. `--chains ethereum,bsc`) - do NOT use `--chain`; `defi position-detail` uses `--chain` (singular) - do NOT use `--chains`.

Before reporting completion: verify the selected command actually succeeded, apply the output format and safety checks from its routed reference, and explicitly report any partial or failed on-chain step.

Run preflight once per conversation/task thread before the first CLI command needing it; do not rerun for later turns/sub-operations; rerun only when the CLI requires it, the previous preflight asks for a retry, or the user explicitly asks to recheck/update.

Invest = multi-chain DeFi product discovery and investment execution; the CLI handles precision conversion, multi-step orchestration and validation internally.

Invest command set: support-chains, support-platforms, list (top products by APY), search, detail (full product details), invest (one-step deposit: CLI handles prepare + precision + calldata), withdraw (one-step withdrawal: CLI handles position lookup + calldata), collect (one-step reward claim: CLI handles reward check + calldata), rate-chart (APY history), tvl-chart (TVL history), depth-price-chart (V3 pool depth or price history). The high-level invest/withdraw/collect are the recommended write path.
`defi positions` / `defi position-detail` belong to the Portfolio capability but are called in Invest as MANDATORY pre-steps before withdraw/collect.

units.source: references/invest.md#Investment Types; references/invest-cli-reference.md#4. onchainos defi search
units.text: productGroup values: SINGLE_EARN = single-token yield (savings, staking, vaults) [search default]; DEX_POOL = liquidity pools (Uniswap V2/V3, PancakeSwap, etc.); LENDING = lending/borrowing (Aave, Compound, etc.).

Deposit flow: 1) `defi search --token USDC --chain ethereum` -> pick investmentId; 2) `defi detail --investment-id <id>` -> confirm APY/TVL, get underlyingToken[].tokenAddress; 3) `token search --query <tokenAddress> --chains <chain>` -> get decimal; 4) ask user for amount, convert userAmount x 10^decimal (100 USDC -> 100000000); 5) check wallet balance (okx-agentic-wallet), if insufficient warn and stop; 6) `defi invest --investment-id <id> --address <addr> --token USDC --amount 100000000` -> CLI returns calldata (APPROVE + DEPOSIT steps); 7) user signs and broadcasts each step in order.
Token decimal lookup: take tokenAddress from `defi detail` -> underlyingToken[].tokenAddress, then `token search --query <tokenAddress>` to get `decimal` (same approach as DEX swap).
units.note: `defi detail` also returns underlyingToken[].tokenPrecision directly, and invest-specific notes say tokenPrecision can come from detail or position-detail.

units.text: `defi invest --amount` must be an integer in MINIMAL units: userAmount x 10^tokenPrecision (e.g. 0.1 USDC, precision 6 -> `--amount 100000`; 100 USDC -> 100000000). Get tokenPrecision from `defi detail` or `defi position-detail`. Decimal/UI-unit values are rejected.
units.note: Verified in upstream Rust: validate_amount rejects any "." and zero/empty.

units.text: CRITICAL - balance check REQUIRED before `defi invest`: verify via okx-agentic-wallet that the user has sufficient balance of the deposit token BEFORE generating calldata. If insufficient, STOP and warn the user; never proceed to `defi invest` without confirmed balance (skipping wastes gas and yields failed on-chain txs).
CRITICAL - `defi position-detail` is MANDATORY immediately before every `defi withdraw`, even if position data was fetched earlier. Never reuse stale position-detail results.

Withdraw flow: 1) `defi positions --address <addr> --chains ethereum`; 2) `defi position-detail --address <addr> --chain ethereum --platform-id <pid>` (fresh) -> investmentId, tokenPrecision, coinAmount (current balance); 3) full exit: `defi withdraw --investment-id <id> --address <addr> --chain ethereum --ratio 1 --platform-id <pid>`; partial exit: `defi withdraw ... --amount <minimal_units> --platform-id <pid>`; 4) user signs and broadcasts.
Partial exit --amount: position-detail returns coinAmount human-readable (e.g. "2.3792") and tokenPrecision (e.g. 6); convert with floor: floor(2.3792 x 10^6) = 2379200 -> `--amount 2379200`.
units.note: Upstream CLI --help text says "Human-readable partial withdrawal amount", but Rust cmd_withdraw calls validate_amount (integer minimal units) - the skill doc is correct. CLI also requires --platform-id with --amount, rejects amount > current balance, and requires --ratio or --amount for non-V3.

units.text: CRITICAL - `defi position-detail` is MANDATORY immediately before every `defi collect`, even if position data exists from earlier in the conversation: rewards, investmentId, platformId and tokenId change after each on-chain operation (withdraw, previous collect), so stale data gives wrong params or failed txs. Never skip; never reuse earlier results.

Claim flow: 1) `defi positions --address <addr> --chains ethereum`; 2) `defi position-detail --address <addr> --chain ethereum --platform-id <pid>` (fresh); 3) `defi collect --address <addr> --chain ethereum --reward-type REWARD_INVESTMENT --investment-id <id> --platform-id <pid>` -> CLI returns calldata, or skips if there are no rewards; 4) user signs and broadcasts.

V3 Pool deposit flow: 1) `defi search --token USDT --platform PancakeSwap --chain bsc --product-group DEX_POOL`; 2) `defi detail --investment-id <id>`; 3) optional `defi depth-price-chart --investment-id <id>` to show liquidity distribution for choosing tick range; 4) ask user for amount and tick range; 5) check wallet balance (okx-agentic-wallet), stop if insufficient; 6) `defi invest --investment-id <id> --address <addr> --token USDT --amount 100000000 --range 5` -> CLI runs calculate-entry internally, returns calldata; 7) user signs and broadcasts.
units.note: CLI help: --range = price range % around current price (5 = +/-5%), required for V3 if --tick-lower/--tick-upper not given; --token2/--amount2 for dual-token V3 entry (amount2 may be 0 for single-sided); --token-id adds to an existing V3 position.

units.source: references/invest.md#View Chart Data; references/invest-cli-reference.md#11. onchainos defi rate-chart
units.text: APY history (check yield trend before depositing): `defi rate-chart --investment-id <id> --time-range MONTH`. Time ranges: WEEK (default), MONTH, SEASON (3 months), YEAR; DAY is V3 Pool only. Returns array of {timestamp (ms), rate (APY = base + mining), bonusRate (extra reward APY: OKX Bonus / Merkl), limitValue (1 = peak, -1 = trough, null = normal), totalReward (fee + bonus reward for period)}.

units.source: references/invest.md#View Chart Data; references/invest-cli-reference.md#12. onchainos defi tvl-chart
units.text: TVL history (evaluate pool size stability): `defi tvl-chart --investment-id <id> --time-range SEASON`. Same time ranges as rate-chart. Returns data object {chartVos[]: {timestamp (ms), tvl (USD), limitValue (1/-1/null)}, text (nullable description)}.

units.source: references/invest.md#View Chart Data; references/invest-cli-reference.md#13. onchainos defi depth-price-chart
units.text: V3 depth chart (V3 Pool only): `defi depth-price-chart --investment-id <id>` (chart-type DEPTH default). Returns per tick {tick, liquidity, liquidityNet, token0Price, token1Price}. DEPTH always returns the current snapshot; --time-range has no effect. Use before a V3 deposit to see where liquidity concentrates and pick tickLower/tickUpper.

units.source: references/invest.md#View Chart Data; references/invest-cli-reference.md#13. onchainos defi depth-price-chart
units.text: V3 price history: `defi depth-price-chart --investment-id <id> --chart-type PRICE --time-range WEEK`. Chart types DEPTH (default) | PRICE; --time-range only applies to PRICE: DAY (default) | WEEK. Returns {token0Price, token1Price, timestamp (ms)} per point.
Use chart commands to analyze product trends before investing or to monitor existing positions.

Path A (user-provided/external wallet), for each dataList step in order: 1) user signs externally using dataList[N].to, dataList[N].serializedData, dataList[N].value; 2) `gateway broadcast --signed-tx <signed_hex> --address <addr> --chain <chain>`; 3) poll `gateway orders --address <addr> --chain <chain> --order-id <orderId>` until txStatus=2, then proceed to next step.

Path B (Agentic Wallet) per dataList step. EVM (Ethereum, BSC, Polygon, Arbitrum, Base, XLayer=196, ...): `wallet contract-call --to <dataList[N].to> --chain <chainIndex> --input-data <dataList[N].serializedData> --amt <dataList[N].valueNormalized> --biz-type defi`. Solana: `wallet contract-call --to <dataList[N].to> --chain 501 --unsigned-tx <dataList[N].serializedData> --biz-type defi`. contract-call does TEE signing and broadcasting internally - no separate broadcast step.
units.note: Sui serializedData is base64 BCS; lite contract-call exposes --sui-tx-bytes but the upstream defi doc gives no Sui Path B recipe.

units.text: CRITICAL - prepared transaction data is opaque: for each dataList[N], use to, serializedData and any applicable value field directly from that same entry. Never recreate, edit, truncate, pad, concatenate, re-encode or annotate a returned transaction field; pass the complete serializedData through the chain-specific argument.

units.source: references/invest.md#Sign & Broadcast Calldata; references/invest-cli-reference.md#7. onchainos defi deposit
units.text: `--amt` = dataList[N].valueNormalized passed directly: already a minimal-unit decimal integer string computed by the CLI (hex -> decimal; ""/null/"0x0" -> "0"). No conversion. If a step carries valueNormalizeError (value unparseable; valueNormalized then "0", not guessed), do NOT execute that step - relay the error and stop.
--chain for `wallet contract-call` and `gateway broadcast` must be the realChainIndex (1 = Ethereum, 137 = Polygon, 56 = BSC, 501 = Solana, 196 = XLayer).

units.source: references/invest.md#Sign & Broadcast Calldata > Execution rules; references/invest-cli-reference.md#7. onchainos defi deposit
units.text: dataList execution: run dataList[0], then dataList[1], ... strictly in array order, never in parallel. Wait for on-chain confirmation before the next step (Path A: txStatus=2; Path B: contract-call returns txHash). If any step fails, stop all remaining steps and report which succeeded and which failed.
`invest` / `withdraw` / `collect` only return UNSIGNED calldata - they do not broadcast; the CLI never holds private keys.
Search/list results table columns: # | Platform | Chain | investmentId | Name | APY | TVL (example: 1 | Aave V3 | ETH | 9502 | USDC | 1.89% | $3.52B).
investmentId is MANDATORY in every search/list row.

units.source: references/invest.md#Displaying Search / List Results; references/invest-cli-reference.md#4. onchainos defi search
units.text: `rate` is a decimal APY -> multiply by 100 and append "%" ("0.01820" = 1.82%); `tvl` (USD) -> human-readable USD ($3.52B, $537M).
Display data as-is - do NOT editorialize on APY values.

units.source: references/invest.md#rewardType Reference; references/invest-cli-reference.md#9. onchainos defi claim
units.text: `defi collect --reward-type` values and required params: REWARD_PLATFORM (protocol-level rewards, e.g. AAVE token from Aave safety module) -> --platform-id; REWARD_INVESTMENT (product mining/staking rewards) -> --investment-id + --platform-id; V3_FEE (Uniswap V3 / PancakeSwap V3 trading fees) -> --investment-id + --token-id; REWARD_OKX_BONUS (OKX bonus) -> --investment-id + --platform-id; REWARD_MERKLE_BONUS (Merkle proof-based bonus / airdrop claims) -> --investment-id + --platform-id; UNLOCKED_PRINCIPAL (principal unlocked after lock period) -> --investment-id + --principal-index.

units.source: references/invest.md#Key Protocol Rules; references/invest-cli-reference.md#7. onchainos defi deposit
units.text: Aave borrow returns callDataType=WITHDRAW (borrow = withdraw from pool) and Aave repay returns callDataType=DEPOSIT (repay = deposit back) - normal Aave internal semantics; do NOT expose these callDataType labels to the user.
Withdraw parameter choice: V3 Pool exit -> `--token-id` + `--ratio` (`--ratio 1` = full exit); partial withdrawal (non-V3) -> `--amount`; full withdrawal -> `--ratio 1`.
units.note: Verified in Rust: V3 path bails without --ratio; product with isSupportRedeem=false bails.

units.text: Post-execution suggestions: after list/search -> view detail (`defi detail`) or start deposit flow; after detail -> check trends (`defi rate-chart` / `defi tvl-chart`) or proceed to `defi invest`; after detail of a V3 Pool -> `defi depth-price-chart` (depth) and `defi depth-price-chart --chart-type PRICE`; after invest success -> view positions (Portfolio) or search more; after withdraw success -> check positions (Portfolio) or balance (okx-agentic-wallet); after collect success -> check positions or swap rewards (okx-agentic-wallet).

units.source: references/invest.md#Invest-specific Notes; references/invest-cli-reference.md#7. onchainos defi deposit
units.text: --slippage default "0.01" (1%); "0.1" = 10%. Suggest "0.03"-"0.05" for volatile V3 pools.

CRITICAL - Solana transaction expiry: Solana DeFi txs are base58 VersionedTransactions whose blockhash expires in ~60 seconds. After receiving Solana calldata you MUST warn: "This Solana transaction must be signed and broadcast within 60 seconds or it will expire. Please sign immediately." Deliver this warning before moving on to anything else.

CRITICAL - high APY warning: when displaying search/list results, if any product has APY > 50% (rate > 0.5), you MUST warn: "WARNING: This product shows APY above 50%, which indicates elevated risk (potential impermanent loss, smart contract risk, or unsustainable rewards). Proceed with caution." Never silently display high-APY products.
User confirmation is required before every invest / withdraw / collect execution.
The address used for calldata generation MUST match the signing address.

The CLI reference claims "all 15 DeFi commands" but documents 13 here (support-chains, support-platforms, list, search, detail, prepare, deposit, redeem, claim, calculate-entry, rate-chart, tvl-chart, depth-price-chart) plus positions/position-detail in portfolio-cli-reference. It does NOT document the high-level invest/withdraw/collect that invest.md flows use; CLI 4.6.3 has 18 defi subcommands. prepare/deposit/redeem/claim/calculate-entry are the low-level path.
units.note: Several low-level examples are stale vs CLI 4.6.3 (see units on deposit/redeem/calculate-entry).

units.text: `defi support-chains` (no params) returns array of {chainIndex (e.g. "1" Ethereum, "56" BSC, "137" POLYGON, "42161" ARBITRUM, "8453" BASE), network (e.g. "ETH", "BSC", "POLYGON")}.
`defi support-platforms` (no params) returns array of {analysisPlatformId (used as --platform-id in other commands), platformName (e.g. "Aave V3", "Lido"), investmentCount}.

units.source: references/invest-cli-reference.md#3. onchainos defi list; references/invest-cli-reference.md#Input / Output Examples
units.text: `defi list [--page-num <n>]`: all products, no filters, sorted by APY descending; page size fixed at 20 (default page 1). Internally the same API as `defi search` with no filters; same return fields as search.

`defi search`: at least one of --token or --platform is REQUIRED (CLI errors if both omitted). --token / --platform take comma-separated keywords ("USDC,ETH", "Aave,Compound"); --chain is a chain name; --product-group defaults to SINGLE_EARN; page size fixed at 20.

search/list return `data` = {total, list[]: {investmentId (used in detail/prepare/deposit), name, platformName, rate (APY decimal string), tvl (USD), chainIndex, feeRate (nullable), detailPath (nullable)}}.

`defi detail --investment-id <id>` returns: investmentId, investmentName, platformName, platformLogo, investType (1=Save, 2=Pool, 3=Farm, 5=Stake, 6=Borrow, ...), chainIndex, network, rate (APY decimal), tvl (USD), feeRate (DEX_POOL only), hasBonus, isSupportClaim, isInvestable, isSupportRedeem, analysisPlatformId (for positions/claim), subscriptionMethod / redeemMethod (DEX_POOL/LENDING only), detailPath, underlyingToken[] {tokenSymbol, tokenAddress, chainIndex, tokenPrecision, tokenLogo}, aboutToken[] {same + marketCap, price}, rateDetails[] {tokenAddress, tokenSymbol, rate, title} (APY breakdown).
units.note: isInvestable / isSupportRedeem / isSupportClaim gate the write commands (Rust withdraw bails when isSupportRedeem=false).

units.text: `defi prepare --investment-id <id>` (pre-investment info) returns investWithTokenList[] {tokenId, tokenSymbol, tokenName, tokenAddress, tokenPrecision, chainIndex, network, coinAmount (current balance), currencyAmount (USD)}; DEX_POOL adds feeRate, currentTick, currentPrice (token0 price ratio), tickSpacing, underlyingTokenList[] (index0 = token0, index1 = token1; tokenId, tokenSymbol, tokenName, tokenLogo, tokenAddress, network, chainIndex, tokenPrecision, isBaseToken = native token).

Low-level `defi deposit --user-input` = JSON array `[{"tokenAddress":"0x...","chainIndex":"1","coinAmount":"50000","tokenPrecision":"6"}]` using tokenAddress, chainIndex, tokenPrecision from `defi prepare` investWithTokenList. coinAmount MUST be minimal units (integer = userAmount x 10^tokenPrecision); tokenPrecision REQUIRED; CLI converts to decimal internally; decimal coinAmount or missing tokenPrecision is rejected.
units.note: Verified in Rust helpers.convert_minimal_to_decimal (also rejects zero/empty). The doc's own "Find top USDC yield" example omits tokenPrecision and would be rejected.

units.source: references/invest-cli-reference.md#7. onchainos defi deposit; references/invest-cli-reference.md#10. onchainos defi calculate-entry
units.text: V3 params: --token-id = V3 NFT tokenId (required to add to an existing V3 position); --tick-lower / --tick-upper required for a NEW V3 position. Use `=` for negative tick values: `--tick-lower=-11`.

Write-command return `data.dataList[]` (execute in order): callDataType, from (user wallet), to (target contract), value (native value, e.g. "0x0"), valueNormalized (minimal-unit decimal string for --amt), valueNormalizeError (only if value unparseable), serializedData (EVM hex 0x / Solana base58 / Sui base64 BCS), originalData (EVM ABI metadata JSON), signatureData (permit, if any), transactionPayload (Aptos JSON), gas (non-EVM only). redeem and claim return the same structure.
callDataType enum: APPROVE (ERC-20 approve), DEPOSIT, SWAP,DEPOSIT (V3: single token into dual-token pool), WITHDRAW, WITHDRAW,SWAP (V3: withdraw then swap back to target token).

serializedData client handling (external signer, Path A): EVM - hex, use as tx.data with `to` as target; Solana - bs58 decode -> skip first 65 bytes (signature placeholder) -> VersionedMessage.deserialize() -> sign -> broadcast within 60 s; Sui - base64 decode -> prepend intent [0,0,0] -> blake2b-256 -> Ed25519 sign -> submit; Aptos - use transactionPayload JSON, build via SDK build.simple() -> sign -> submit.

Low-level `defi redeem --id <id> --address <addr>`: --ratio "1" = 100% / "0.5" = 50% (use "1" for full exit; partial exit uses --user-input); --token/--symbol/--amount/--precision = LP/receipt token single-token shorthand (human-readable amount + decimals); --chain required for LP token input; --token-id = V3 NFT (required for V3 remove liquidity); --user-input JSON `[{"tokenAddress":"<underlying>","chainIndex":"<id>","coinAmount":"<amount>"}]` required for liquid-staking exits (Jito/JitoSOL, Lido/stETH) and other non-lending, non-V3 exits, and takes precedence over --token/--amount; --slippage default "0.01".
units.note: CLI 4.6.3 validates redeem --user-input the same way as deposit (integer minimal coinAmount + tokenPrecision required); the doc format omits tokenPrecision and the Aave example uses "100.23" - stale.

units.text: Redeem rules: always call `defi position-detail` before `defi redeem` (investmentId + underlying token info). Full exit: --ratio 1 (+ --user-input if token info available, preferred). Partial exit: MUST pass --user-input with underlying token address and exact amount. Lending repay: always --user-input with exact repay amount, never --ratio 1. V3 Pool exits: --token-id only, no --user-input or --ratio.
units.note: Conflicts with invest.md Key Protocol Rules ("V3 exit: --token-id + --ratio"), which is for high-level `defi withdraw` (CLI requires --ratio there).

units.text: Common redeem callDataType patterns: [WITHDRAW] standard single-step; [APPROVE, WITHDRAW] aToken approval needed first; [WITHDRAW, SWAP] V3 remove liquidity then swap back; [DEPOSIT] Aave repay.

Low-level `defi claim --address <addr> --reward-type <type>`: --id required for REWARD_INVESTMENT, REWARD_OKX_BONUS, REWARD_MERKLE_BONUS, V3_FEE; --platform-id required for REWARD_PLATFORM and also enables auto-fetch of expectOutputList; --token-id required for V3_FEE; --principal-index required for UNLOCKED_PRINCIPAL; --expect-output JSON `[{"tokenAddress":"0x...","chainIndex":"1","coinAmount":"0.01"}]` - pass directly from position-detail rewardDefiTokenInfo when available (preferred), auto-fetch via --platform-id is the fallback. V3_FEE and UNLOCKED_PRINCIPAL need no --expect-output.

Low-level `defi calculate-entry --id <id> --address <addr> --input-token <addr> --input-amount <amt> --token-decimal <n> [--tick-lower=<n> --tick-upper=<n>]`: must be called after `defi prepare` for V3 pools; user gives one token amount, returns tokenList[] {tokenAddress, tokenSymbol, coinAmount, chainIndex} with exact amounts for BOTH pool tokens, to be used in `defi deposit --user-input`.
units.note: Doc says --input-amount is human-readable ("100"); CLI 4.6.3 requires integer minimal units (rejects "."), and converts output coinAmount to minimal units and adds tokenPrecision. High-level `defi invest --range/--tick-*` runs this internally.

units.source: references/invest-cli-reference.md#Input / Output Examples > Find top USDC yield on Ethereum
units.text: Low-level deposit example: `defi search --token USDC --chain ethereum --product-group SINGLE_EARN` -> `defi detail --investment-id 9502` (check isInvestable) -> `defi prepare --investment-id 9502` (tokenAddress, chainIndex, tokenPrecision) -> `defi deposit --investment-id 9502 --address <addr> --user-input '[...]'` -> dataList -> sign and broadcast via okx-agentic-wallet.
units.note: Example passes coinAmount "100" without tokenPrecision - contradicts the minimal-units + tokenPrecision rule; prefer high-level `defi invest`.

units.source: references/invest-cli-reference.md#Input / Output Examples > V3 Pool entry with calculate-entry
units.text: Low-level V3 entry: `defi search --token USDT --platform PancakeSwap --chain bsc --product-group DEX_POOL` -> `defi prepare` (currentTick, tickSpacing, underlyingTokenList) -> `defi calculate-entry ... --tick-lower=-32150 --tick-upper=-31350` (amounts for both tokens) -> `defi deposit --user-input '[tokenA, tokenB]'` with the same ticks.

units.source: references/invest-cli-reference.md#Input / Output Examples > Redeem full position from Aave
units.text: Low-level full Aave redeem: `defi positions --address <addr> --chains ethereum` (analysisPlatformId e.g. "44" for Aave) -> `defi position-detail --address <addr> --chain ethereum --platform-id 44` (investmentId, coinAmount) -> `defi redeem --id 9502 --chain ethereum --address <addr> --ratio 1 --user-input '[...]'` -> dataList [WITHDRAW] -> sign and broadcast.

Low-level REWARD_INVESTMENT claim: position-detail first (MUST) -> take rewardDefiTokenInfo [{tokenAddress, chainIndex, coinAmount}] -> `defi claim --address <addr> --chain ethereum --reward-type REWARD_INVESTMENT --id 9502 --platform-id 44 --expect-output '[...]'` (direct pass preferred over auto-fetch).

units.source: references/invest-cli-reference.md#Input / Output Examples > Claim V3 trading fees
units.text: Low-level V3 fee claim: `defi position-detail` to get tokenId + investmentId -> `defi claim --address <addr> --chain ethereum --reward-type V3_FEE --id <investmentId> --token-id <tokenId>` (no --expect-output).

units.source: references/invest-cli-reference.md#Input / Output Examples > Check holdings across multiple chains
units.text: Multi-chain holdings: `defi positions --address <addr> --chains ethereum,bsc,avalanche,solana` -> per-chain platform list with totalValue, analysisPlatformId.
units.note: Example mixes a 0x address with solana, contradicting the Address-Chain Compatibility rule (84019); follow the rule and split EVM vs Solana.

units.text: 84400 Parameter null -> check required params; a partial exit needs --amount or --ratio. Also triggered by a decimal/UI-unit --amount.
84021 Asset syncing -> tell the user "Position data is syncing, please retry shortly".
84023 Invalid expectOutputList -> CLI auto-constructs it from position-detail; retry or pass --platform-id.
84014 Balance check failed -> insufficient balance; check with okx-agentic-wallet.
84018 Balancing failed (V3) -> adjust price range or increase slippage.
84010 Token not supported -> check supported tokens via `defi detail`.
84001 Platform not supported -> the DeFi platform is not supported.
84016 Contract execution failed -> check parameters and retry.
84019 Address format mismatch -> --address and chain params incompatible (EVM 0x vs Solana base58 vs Sui/Tron/TON); apply Address-Chain Compatibility and split EVM and Solana into two separate calls.
50011 Rate limit -> wait 1-2 s and retry once; if it persists, tell the user the service is rate-limiting.

CLI-generated payload rejected before submission: if `wallet contract-call` returns `-32602 Invalid params` or a calldata/payload validation error WITHOUT a txHash -> stop and discard the unexecuted dataList; never inspect, edit, re-encode or resubmit the old serializedData; rerun the documented DeFi preparation flow and use only the newly returned fields. If a txHash was returned this rule does not apply - use the wallet transaction-status flow.

Calldata generated but broadcast fails on-chain -> the position changed between position-detail and the write call (another withdraw/claim landed first); re-run `defi position-detail` and regenerate; never reuse stale calldata.
Solana calldata expired (blockhash ~60 s) -> if signing took too long, regenerate the calldata; do not retry the expired payload.
--amount rejected -> must be an integer in minimal units (userAmount x 10^tokenPrecision); a decimal or UI-unit value triggers parameter errors (84400).
Portfolio = read-only viewing of DeFi positions and holdings across protocols and chains (commands: support-chains, support-platforms, positions, position-detail).
Quickstart: `defi positions --address <addr> --chains ethereum,bsc,solana` (overview) then `defi position-detail --address <addr> --chain ethereum --platform-id <analysisPlatformId from positions>`.
units.note: Quickstart mixes EVM chains and solana with one 0x address - contradicts the compatibility rule.

units.text: DeFi chain aliases -> chainIndex: Ethereum ethereum/eth 1; BSC bsc/bnb 56; Polygon polygon/matic 137; Arbitrum arbitrum/arb 42161; Base base 8453; X Layer xlayer/okb 196; Avalanche avalanche/avax 43114; Optimism optimism/op 10; Fantom fantom/ftm 250; Sui sui 784; Tron tron/trx 195; TON ton 607; Linea linea 59144; Scroll scroll 534352; zkSync zksync 324; Solana solana/sol 501.
Portfolio intent: view positions/portfolio/holdings -> `defi positions`; view detail for a protocol -> `defi position-detail`; redeem/claim after viewing -> switch to the Invest capability.

Missing params: address -> address-resolution flow (wallet status -> wallet addresses) or ask if not logged in; chains -> ask which chains or suggest common ones (ethereum, bsc, solana); platform-id -> run `defi positions` first and use its analysisPlatformId (position-detail requires it as --platform-id).

`defi positions` display MUST use exactly these columns in this order, no substitutions/omissions: # | Platform | analysisPlatformId | Chains | Positions | Value(USD) (example: 1 | Aave V3 | 12345 | ETH,BSC | 2 | $120.00).
analysisPlatformId is MANDATORY in every positions row (users copy it for position-detail); never omit, hide, or replace it with another field.
Never group platforms - every platform is its own row regardless of value size.

Positions raw JSON mapping: each element of walletIdPlatformList[*].platformList[*] is one row; platformName -> Platform; analysisPlatformId -> analysisPlatformId; networkBalanceList[*].network joined with comma -> Chains; investmentCount -> Positions; currencyAmount -> Value(USD).
units.note: portfolio-cli-reference lists different per-platform fields (totalValue, investedValue, profitValue, chainIndex, investTypeList, rewardDefiTokenInfo); display mapping here reflects actual API shape.

units.text: `defi position-detail` output shape: {"ok": true, "data": [ {"walletIdPlatformDetailList": [...]}, ... ]} - `data` is an ARRAY; iterate it; calling .get() on data directly is a client-side bug, not an API error.

`defi position-detail` display: ALL tokens in a single flat table with exact columns: Type | Asset | Amount | Value(USD) | investmentId | aggregateProductId | Token Contract | Rewards (e.g. Supply | USDT | 1.002285 | $1.0025 | 127 | 71931 | 0x970223...7 | 0.000080 AVAX; Pending | sAVAX | 0.00000091 | $0.000012 | - | - | - | Platform reward). Each token is one row; merge investmentId and aggregateProductId from its parent investment entry.
investmentId is MANDATORY in every position-detail row (needed for redeem/claim via Invest); aggregateProductId shown if present, else "-".
Token Contract: show the FULL contract address without truncation; "-" if native/empty.
units.note: The doc's own example row shows a truncated address (0x970223...7), contradicting the rule.

units.text: Rewards column: pending reward amount + symbol if present, "-" if none; platform rewards show "Platform reward". Type column: map investType -> Supply/Borrow/Stake/Farm/Pool etc.; pending-rewards rows use "Pending".
Health rate (lending): show separately below the position-detail table, with a warning if healthRate < 1.5.

V3 Pool positions (positionList present): add a section per position with columns tokenId | Status | Range | tickLower | tickUpper, from positionList[].tokenId, positionStatus (ACTIVE | INACTIVE), positionList[].range (e.g. "0.892 - 0.992 USDC/DAI"), positionList[].rangeInfo.tickLower / rangeInfo.tickUpper. These fields are critical for V3 operations (add liquidity, withdraw, collect V3 fees).

units.source: references/portfolio.md#investType Reference; references/portfolio-cli-reference.md#2. onchainos defi position-detail
units.text: investType values: 1 Save (savings/yield), 2 Pool (liquidity pool), 3 Farm (yield farming), 4 Vaults, 5 Stake, 6 Borrow, 7 Staking, 8 Locked, 9 Deposit, 10 Vesting.

Portfolio post-execution suggestions: after `defi positions` -> 1) view detail (`defi position-detail`), 2) redeem (Invest), 3) claim rewards (Invest); after `defi position-detail` -> 1) redeem with investmentId from the table, 2) claim rewards, 3) add more (all Invest); after position-detail of a V3 Pool -> `defi depth-price-chart --investment-id <id>` and `defi depth-price-chart --investment-id <id> --chart-type PRICE`.

`defi positions --address <addr> --chains <comma-separated>` (both required) returns per-platform entries: analysisPlatformId (used by position-detail and claim --platform-id), platformName, chainIndex, totalValue (USD), investedValue (USD), profitValue (unrealized P/L USD), platformLogo, investTypeList[], rewardDefiTokenInfo[] (pending claimable rewards).

`defi position-detail --address <addr> --chain <chain> --platform-id <analysisPlatformId>` (all required) returns per position: investmentId (for redeem/claim), investmentName, investType, coinAmount (current redeemable balance, token units), coinUsdValue, tokenAddress / tokenSymbol (receipt/LP token), apy, earnedTokenList[] (pending rewards), tokenId (V3 NFT; use in redeem --token-id), tickLower, tickUpper, healthRate (LENDING only).
units.note: invest flows also rely on tokenPrecision and rewardDefiTokenInfo from position-detail, which this schema omits.

units.text: --chains vs --chain confusion: passing the wrong one to positions/position-detail is a parameter error, not an empty result.

Empty positions but the user insists they have holdings: check the address/chain pairing first (84019 class), then whether the protocol is supported (`defi support-platforms`); positions on unsupported platforms do not appear.
